newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia may ease prospectus rules - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia may ease prospectus rules - paper.

text.p: Australian Industry Minister John Moore has said small companies should be able to raise equity without an accompanying full prospectus and function under easier reporting requirements, the Australian Financial Review newspaper reported on Monday.

Moore told the newspaper the small business sector needed to be revitalised and as part of the plan directors' fiduciary responsibilities could be reviewed under a proposal to set up a second board on the Australian Stock Exchange.
"The Standards required of some directors these days are getting far too high," Moore told the newspaper in an interview.
"I would like to see them maintaining the same standards, but you would have to be realistic about their reporting requirements," Moore said.
He said small companies would have to be relied on to report with honesty and integrity.
"You should be able to produce a prospectus which is vastly cheaper, it might well be a memorandum of sale, and you don't have to meet all the half-yearly, or quarterly reporting standards," he said.
The memo of sale would provide investors with minimal information instead of issuing a full due diligence prospectus, marking the memo 'buyer beware.'
"We used to be able to do it on three or four sheets of paper."
"These days for a relatively small capital raising, half (a million) to A$2 million, the expense of a full due diligence prospectus really isn't warranted."
